The Bluecheek silver grunt, Pomadasys argyreus, exhibits life-history traits typical of many haemulid fishes inhabiting tropical coastal waters. Field surveys indicate that individuals can ultimately attain a total length of 40 centimeters [Li = 40 centimeters], representing the maximum size recorded for this species within its range. Growth analyses based on length-frequency data suggest that this asymptotic size is approached after several years of sustained feeding. The wet weight of a fully grown adult, derived from length-weight regressions, approaches 912 grams [Wwi = 912 grams], a value that reflects the robust, laterally compressed body form characteristic of the genus. In contrast, the onset of reproductive capability occurs considerably earlier. Examination of gonadal development in specimens collected from the Arabian Gulf has shown that puberty is first achieved at a total length of 13.5 centimeters [Lp = 13.5 centimeters], at which point individuals weigh approximately 33.9 grams [Wwp = approximately 33.9 grams]. This size at maturity represents a relatively small fraction of the ultimate body size, a pattern often associated with species that experience high rates of natural mortality early in life.

Reproductive output in Pomadasys argyreus has been quantified through histological examination of ovaries from gravid females captured in their natural habitat. During the peak spawning months from May through September, females held at a stable water temperature of 28.4 °C [T = 28.4 °C] have been documented to release an average of 43,182 ova per spawning event [N_R_i = 43,182 ova per spawning event]. Over the five-month spawning season, this translates to approximately 5 spawning events per year [F_R_i = approximately 5 spawning events per year], indicating a high fecundity strategy, likely an adaptation to the unpredictable survival conditions faced by pelagic larvae. The maintenance of such high fecundity requires consistent access to abundant food resources throughout the protracted breeding season.

The early life stages of the Bluecheek silver grunt are characterized by a brief incubation period and rapid transition to exogenous feeding. Fertilized eggs, which are pelagic and transparent, hatch after approximately 3.3 days [ab = approximately 3.3 days] when incubated at a temperature of 28.4 °C [T = 28.4 °C]. This rapid embryonic development reduces the window of vulnerability for the yolk-dependent embryo to predation and microbial infection in the water column. The newly emerged yolk-sac larva, or prolarva, is minute and initially completely dependent on its endogenous yolk reserves. Based on an egg diameter of 0.4 millimeters, the calculated wet weight at the moment of hatching is 0.0000335 grams [Wwb = 0.0000335 grams]. This extremely low birth mass places the species firmly among those producing small, numerous offspring, a classic r-selected life-history strategy that prioritizes high fecundity over individual offspring size, a pattern commonly observed in other haemulid fishes such as Pomadasys kaakan. The larvae remain in a lecithotrophic state for a very short period before commencing first exogenous feeding.

Longevity estimates for Pomadasys argyreus are derived from analysis of growth increments in hard structures such as otoliths. These studies indicate a maximum lifespan of 4,380 days [am = 4,380 days] for individuals inhabiting waters with a mean annual temperature of 28.4 °C [T = 28.4 °C]. This lifespan of approximately twelve years is consistent with the moderate longevity observed in many congeneric species that occupy similar shallow-water, demersal habitats. The age at birth is effectively instantaneous, meaning that the 3.3-day incubation period (3.3 days) [ab = 3.3 days] at 28.4 °C [T = 28.4 °C] represents the very earliest post-fertilization stage considered here. The completion of the life cycle, from the hatching of the tiny prolarva to the death of a senescent adult, thus spans a period of over a decade, allowing multiple reproductive seasons and contributing to population stability through iteroparity.

The body size at which Pomadasys argyreus begins its reproductive life represents a key demographic parameter. At a total length of 13.5 centimeters [Lp = 13.5 centimeters], a female achieves a wet body mass of 33.9 grams [Wwp = 33.9 grams], a value that marks the transition from juvenile growth to the allocation of resources toward gametogenesis. This pubertal mass is only a small fraction, roughly 3.7 percent, of the ultimate adult weight of 912 grams [Wwi = 912 grams] that can be attained by a 40 centimeter [Li = 40 centimeter] individual. Such a disparity between size at maturity and asymptotic size suggests that the species experiences a prolonged adult growth phase, during which fecundity likely increases with body size in accordance with the length-weight relationship. Larger, older females thus make a disproportionately large contribution to the overall reproductive output of the population, highlighting the importance of iteroparity in maintaining population stability.
